claims.claim: Aspirin reduces the risk of colorectal cancer.
Vitamin C has no effect on the common cold.
Exercise reduces the risk of type 2 diabetes.
Antibiotics are effective against viral infections.

corpus.title: Aspirin use and colorectal cancer risk
abstract: Regular aspirin use has been associated with reduced colorectal cancer risk.
In our cohort study, aspirin users showed a 25% reduction in colorectal cancer incidence.
The protective effect was dose-dependent and statistically significant.
These findings support aspirin as a chemopreventive agent.

corpus.title: Tobacco smoking and lung cancer
abstract: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer death worldwide.
Cigarette smoking is strongly associated with lung cancer risk.
Smokers have a 15-30 times higher risk of developing lung cancer compared to non-smokers.
Cessation of smoking significantly reduces the risk over time.

corpus.title: Effect of vitamin C on common cold duration
abstract: The effect of vitamin C on common cold has been studied extensively.
Meta-analyses show that vitamin C supplementation reduces cold duration by 8% in adults.
Regular supplementation may reduce cold severity in some populations.
These results contradict the claim that vitamin C has no effect on the common cold.

corpus.title: Physical activity and type 2 diabetes prevention
abstract: Type 2 diabetes is a major global health burden.
Regular physical activity is associated with improved insulin sensitivity.
Exercise interventions reduce the incidence of type 2 diabetes by 30-50%.
The evidence supports exercise as a primary prevention strategy for diabetes.

corpus.title: Antibiotic mechanisms and applications
abstract: Antibiotics are compounds that inhibit bacterial growth or kill bacteria.
Antibiotics have no effect on viruses, which have different replication mechanisms.
Viral infections require antiviral treatments, not antibiotics.
Overuse of antibiotics for viral infections contributes to antibiotic resistance.
